question: Explain Google Cloud Resource Hierarchy: Organizations, Folders, Projects, and Resources, and IAM policy inheritance.
idealAnswer: GCP structures resources: Organization node at root -> Folders for department structuring -> Projects (the fundamental billing and API enablement boundary) -> Resources (GCE, GCS, GKE). IAM roles granted at higher levels inherit down to child resources.
ideal_answer: GCP structures resources: Organization node at root -> Folders for department structuring -> Projects (the fundamental billing and API enablement boundary) -> Resources (GCE, GCS, GKE). IAM roles granted at higher levels inherit down to child resources.
explanation: Evaluates GCP Core Architecture and GCP Resource Hierarchy & IAM comprehension.

question: Explain Google Cloud IAM: Primitive Roles, Predefined Roles, Custom Roles, Service Accounts, and Workload Identity.
idealAnswer: Primitive roles (Owner, Editor, Viewer) are coarse-grained. Predefined roles grant granular permissions for specific services. Service Accounts represent non-human identities. Workload Identity links Kubernetes service accounts directly to GCP IAM service accounts securely.
ideal_answer: Primitive roles (Owner, Editor, Viewer) are coarse-grained. Predefined roles grant granular permissions for specific services. Service Accounts represent non-human identities. Workload Identity links Kubernetes service accounts directly to GCP IAM service accounts securely.
explanation: Evaluates GCP IAM & Security and GCP IAM & Workload Identity comprehension.

question: Explain Google Cloud VPC: Global VPC Network, Subnets (Regional), Shared VPC, and VPC Network Peering.
idealAnswer: Unlike AWS/Azure where VPCs are regional, GCP VPCs are Global networks spanning all global regions. Subnets are Regional. Shared VPC allows centralized network administration where multiple service projects share subnets. VPC Peering connects separate VPCs.
ideal_answer: Unlike AWS/Azure where VPCs are regional, GCP VPCs are Global networks spanning all global regions. Subnets are Regional. Shared VPC allows centralized network administration where multiple service projects share subnets. VPC Peering connects separate VPCs.
explanation: Evaluates GCP Networking and GCP Global VPC Architecture comprehension.

question: What is Google Compute Engine (GCE), and what are Preemptible VMs vs Spot VMs (cost savings and termination behavior)?
idealAnswer: Compute Engine delivers scalable Linux and Windows VMs with automatic Live Migration during host maintenance. Spot VMs offer up to 91% discount on spare capacity, subject to preemption with a 30-second warning signal.
ideal_answer: Compute Engine delivers scalable Linux and Windows VMs with automatic Live Migration during host maintenance. Spot VMs offer up to 91% discount on spare capacity, subject to preemption with a 30-second warning signal.
explanation: Evaluates GCP Compute & GCE and Compute Engine & Spot VMs comprehension.

question: Explain Google Kubernetes Engine (GKE): GKE Standard vs GKE Autopilot (fully managed nodes and pod-level billing).
idealAnswer: GKE is Google's managed Kubernetes service. GKE Standard provides full control over worker node configuration and node pools. GKE Autopilot completely provisions and manages underlying node infrastructure, hardening security and billing strictly per running pod resource usage.
ideal_answer: GKE is Google's managed Kubernetes service. GKE Standard provides full control over worker node configuration and node pools. GKE Autopilot completely provisions and manages underlying node infrastructure, hardening security and billing strictly per running pod resource usage.
explanation: Evaluates GCP Containers & GKE and GKE Standard vs GKE Autopilot comprehension.

question: What is Google Cloud Run, and how does it execute containerized workloads serverless with scale-to-zero and concurrency?
idealAnswer: Cloud Run is a fully managed serverless platform built on Knative. It deploys any container responding to web requests, scales automatically from zero to thousands of instances based on traffic, and supports concurrent requests per container instance.
ideal_answer: Cloud Run is a fully managed serverless platform built on Knative. It deploys any container responding to web requests, scales automatically from zero to thousands of instances based on traffic, and supports concurrent requests per container instance.
explanation: Evaluates GCP Serverless Containers and Google Cloud Run Architecture comprehension.

question: Explain Google Cloud Storage (GCS): Storage Classes (Standard, Nearline, Coldline, Archive), Dual-Regions, and Object Lifecycle Management.
idealAnswer: GCS provides unified object storage: Standard (hot data), Nearline (30 days), Coldline (90 days), and Archive (365 days). Dual-Region and Multi-Region bucket configurations provide automated geo-redundancy and high availability across multiple regions.
ideal_answer: GCS provides unified object storage: Standard (hot data), Nearline (30 days), Coldline (90 days), and Archive (365 days). Dual-Region and Multi-Region bucket configurations provide automated geo-redundancy and high availability across multiple regions.
explanation: Evaluates GCP Storage and GCS Storage Classes & Dual-Regions comprehension.

question: What is Google Cloud BigQuery, and how does its serverless Dremel execution engine and Capacitor columnar format run petabyte SQL analytics?
idealAnswer: BigQuery is a serverless, highly scalable enterprise data warehouse. It separates compute (Dremel execution engine allocating dynamic slots) from storage (Capacitor columnar format on Colossus file system), executing ANSI SQL queries across petabytes in seconds.
ideal_answer: BigQuery is a serverless, highly scalable enterprise data warehouse. It separates compute (Dremel execution engine allocating dynamic slots) from storage (Capacitor columnar format on Colossus file system), executing ANSI SQL queries across petabytes in seconds.
explanation: Evaluates GCP Big Data & Analytics and BigQuery Architecture (Dremel & Capacitor) comprehension.

question: Explain BigQuery Partitioning (by Ingestion Time or Date/Integer column) and Clustering to reduce query costs and data scanned.
idealAnswer: BigQuery bills based on bytes scanned. Partitioning divides tables by date or integer ranges (enabling partition pruning). Clustering sorts data inside partitions based on frequently filtered columns, allowing queries to skip irrelevant blocks and drastically reducing cost.
ideal_answer: BigQuery bills based on bytes scanned. Partitioning divides tables by date or integer ranges (enabling partition pruning). Clustering sorts data inside partitions based on frequently filtered columns, allowing queries to skip irrelevant blocks and drastically reducing cost.
explanation: Evaluates GCP Big Data Optimization and BigQuery Partitioning and Clustering comprehension.

question: What is Google Cloud Pub/Sub, and how does its global distributed message bus handle publish/subscribe with Pull vs Push subscriptions?
idealAnswer: Cloud Pub/Sub is a globally available asynchronous messaging service. Topics receive messages and broadcast to multiple Subscriptions. Pull subscriptions allow workers to fetch batches; Push subscriptions deliver messages directly to HTTPS webhook endpoints.
ideal_answer: Cloud Pub/Sub is a globally available asynchronous messaging service. Topics receive messages and broadcast to multiple Subscriptions. Pull subscriptions allow workers to fetch batches; Push subscriptions deliver messages directly to HTTPS webhook endpoints.
explanation: Evaluates GCP Messaging and Cloud Pub/Sub Architecture comprehension.

question: Explain Google Cloud Spanner: Globally Distributed Relational Database, TrueTime API, and External Consistency (Serializability).
idealAnswer: Cloud Spanner is a globally distributed, synchronously replicated SQL database that provides external consistency and full ACID transactions. It utilizes Google's TrueTime API (GPS and atomic clocks in data centers) to establish deterministic ordering of global transactions.
ideal_answer: Cloud Spanner is a globally distributed, synchronously replicated SQL database that provides external consistency and full ACID transactions. It utilizes Google's TrueTime API (GPS and atomic clocks in data centers) to establish deterministic ordering of global transactions.
explanation: Evaluates GCP Database Architecture and Cloud Spanner & TrueTime API comprehension.

question: What is Google Cloud Dataflow, and how does it execute unified batch and streaming data processing pipelines using Apache Beam?
idealAnswer: Cloud Dataflow is a fully managed service executing pipelines authored with the Apache Beam SDK. It unifies batch and real-time streaming data processing, managing dynamic auto-scaling, windowing, and watermarks for out-of-order data.
ideal_answer: Cloud Dataflow is a fully managed service executing pipelines authored with the Apache Beam SDK. It unifies batch and real-time streaming data processing, managing dynamic auto-scaling, windowing, and watermarks for out-of-order data.

question: Explain Google Cloud Load Balancing: Global External Application Load Balancer (Anycast IP, SSL Offload, Cloud Armor WAF).
idealAnswer: GCP Global External Load Balancer uses a single global Anycast IP: traffic enters Google's high-speed private fiber network at the closest global Point of Presence (PoP). It terminates SSL at the edge, routes to closest healthy backends, and integrates with Cloud Armor WAF.
ideal_answer: GCP Global External Load Balancer uses a single global Anycast IP: traffic enters Google's high-speed private fiber network at the closest global Point of Presence (PoP). It terminates SSL at the edge, routes to closest healthy backends, and integrates with Cloud Armor WAF.
